newsitem.title: GERMANY: Deutsche takes responsibility for MGAM unit trusts.
newsitem.headline: Deutsche takes responsibility for MGAM unit trusts.

text.p: Deutsche Bank AG said on Thursday its German fund management unit DWS was taking over ultimate managerial responsibility for the unit trust business of London-based Morgan Grenfell Asset Management (MGAM).
Deutsche's decision follows problems at three MGAM funds in September which prompted the bank to consider afresh plans to put its British unit trust business under Frankfurt's supervision.
"Ultimate responsibility for MGAM unit trusts will lie with DWS," Deutsche management board member Tessen von Heydebreck told a news conference. "We at DWS will have risk control."
Heydebreck said DWS, or Deutsche Gesellschaft fuer Wertpapiersparen mbH, would not take responsibility for MGAM's institutional funds business.
Deutsche Morgan Grenfell last month announced the departure of four key managers following a probe into irregularities at its unit trust business.

Their departures follow revelations of major problems in the MGAM funds in September. The discovery of misvaluations of speculative unlisted stocks led to the temporary suspension of the funds and a 180 million pound cash injection by Deutsche to shore them up.

Heydebreck also said Deutsche expected Britain's investments watchdog IMRO, which is conducting its own investigation into the affair, to reach a decision by year-end on whether investors are due compensation for the loss of value of the three funds.
"We are in the most intensive discussions with IMRO and we both have the firm intention to see this resolved by the end of the year," Heydebreck said.
If IMRO, the Investment Management Regulatory Organisation, finds that MGAM breached rules, it could lead to hefty fines and possible action against individuals.
